sentences.text: Researchers used a genetic screening method in mice to remove specific genes and assess their impact on natural killer cell growth, subsequently testing immune profiles and infecting the animals with a mouse-specific virus.

This screen identified genes controlling natural killer cell development, including those managing cell movement and gene activity, while infection tests revealed that synaptotagmin-like protein 3 helps these cells release their contents to fight viruses.

In large databases of human DNA, these genes showed signs that losing their function is harmful, and they were also linked to lower counts of natural killer cells in a group of patients with weak immune systems.
